raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Motivation

On XPU, `ScaleResidualLayerNormScaleShift.forward_xpu` runs a triton kernel that blocks regional `torch.compile` of a Wan2.2 DiT block. Inductor re-lowers the kernel and Intel triton fails to compile the result:

```
triton/backends/intel/compiler.py: make_llir -> RuntimeError: PassManager::run failed
```

This happens in the first denoise step, so compiled Wan2.2 cannot run on XPU today. sgl-kernel-xpu ships an AOT SYCL kernel for the same op (sgl-project/sgl-kernel-xpu#497), in the `sglang-kernel-xpu` 0.4.0 wheel already pinned in `pyproject_xpu.toml`. It is a registered custom op, so inductor keeps it opaque and compiled regions call it unchanged.

## Modifications

- `kernels/ops/diffusion/norm/scale_residual_norm_scale_shift_sycl.py` (new): the SYCL backend, exported through the `ops.diffusion` facade.
  - `can_use_fused_scale_residual_norm_scale_shift_sycl` reuses the triton eligibility check for shape, device and contiguity, and adds the kernel's dtype rule. Gate, weight and bias must share one dtype. Scale and shift are cast to it only when the cast is exact (same dtype, or an upcast to fp32); any other mix stays on triton.
  - `fused_scale_residual_norm_scale_shift_sycl` calls `torch.ops.sgl_kernel` directly, so operands are validated once by the op's C++ checks.
  - A `register_fake` companion lets Dynamo trace the op, since sgl-kernel-xpu registers only the XPU implementation.
- `layernorm.py`: `forward_xpu` prefers the SYCL kernel, then triton, then `forward_native`. The import sits in the existing `_is_xpu` block next to `fused_inplace_qknorm_rope`, so other platforms never load it.

No model code changes. Wan's self-attention site passes bf16 1-element null shift/scale next to an fp32 gate and fp32 affine parameters. The exact upcast keeps that site on the SYCL path, so other devices see no change.

## Accuracy Tests

<!-- Wan2.2-I2V-A14B, same command and seed as the speed tests. Outputs compared frame by frame:

| Comparison | Result |
|---|---|
| Same commit, two runs (before, and after) | bit-identical |
| Before (triton) vs after (SYCL), eager | 29.5 dB PSNR, pixel std 65.7 in both |
| After, compiled vs eager | 30.8 dB PSNR, pixel std 65.7 in both |

The cross-backend gap is expected numerical drift between two fp32-math kernels over 20 denoise steps, not a quality change. At the kernel level, at the Wan shape `[1, 17160, 5120]` bf16 with fp32 parameters, the max abs error against `forward_native` is 0.062 on `y` and 0.053 on the residual output.
-->

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Wan2.2-I2V-A14B, TP=4 on 4x Arc Pro B60, 832x480 resolution, 21 frames, 20 steps, warm caches, first run of the session discarded:

```bash
CCL_ZE_IPC_EXCHANGE=pidfd sglang generate \
  --model-path Wan-AI/Wan2.2-I2V-A14B-Diffusers --num-gpus 4 --tp-size 4 \
  --text-encoder-cpu-offload --pin-cpu-memory \
  --image-path <i2v_input.JPG> --prompt "<prompt>" \
  --height 480 --width 832 --num-frames 21 --num-inference-steps 20 --seed 42 \
  [--enable-torch-compile --regional-compile]   # SGLANG_TORCH_COMPILE_MODE=default
```

| Mode | Denoise before (s) | Denoise after (s) |
|---|---|---|
| eager | 100.43 / 100.10 | 100.10 / 100.05 |
| regional compile | fails at step 0 | 82.74 / 82.74 |

- Eager is unchanged. Both kernels cost about 1.8 ms per call on the GPU at the Wan shape, and the host queues all steps well ahead of the device.
- Regional compile now runs, and its denoise time is 17% below eager (1.21x).
- Compiled end-to-end time is still higher than eager because `--enable-torch-compile` also compiles `vae.decode`. That is unrelated to this PR.


## Checklist

- [ ] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [ ] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations).
- [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [ ] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

## Review and Merge Process

1. Ping Merge Oncalls to start the process. See the [PR Merge Process](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/MAINTAINER.md#pull-request-merge-process).
2. Get approvals from [CODEOWNERS](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/CODEOWNERS) and other reviewers.
3. Trigger CI tests with [comments](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#how-to-trigger-ci-tests) or contact authorized users to do so.
   - Common commands include `/tag-and-rerun-ci`, `/tag-run-ci-label`, `/rerun-failed-ci`
4. After green CI and required approvals, ask Merge Oncalls or people with Write permission to merge the PR.

@@ -0,0 +1,78 @@
+import torch
+from sgl_kernel.diffusion import (
+    MAX_FUSED_HIDDEN,
+)
+from sgl_kernel.diffusion import (  # noqa: F401  re-exported via ops.diffusion
+    fused_scale_residual_norm_scale_shift as fused_scale_residual_norm_scale_shift_sycl,
+)
+
+from sglang.srt.utils.patch_torch import register_fake_if_exists
+
+_SUPPORTED_DTYPES = (torch.float32, torch.float16, torch.bfloat16)
+
+
+def can_use_fused_scale_residual_norm_scale_shift_sycl(
+    *,
+    residual: torch.Tensor,
+    x: torch.Tensor,
+    gate: torch.Tensor | int,
+    shift: torch.Tensor,
+    scale: torch.Tensor,
+    weight: torch.Tensor | None,
+    bias: torch.Tensor | None,
+) -> bool:
+    # sgl_kernel's wrapper raises on unsupported operands; this lets the caller
+    # fall back to triton or eager instead.
+    if x.device.type != "xpu" or x.dtype not in _SUPPORTED_DTYPES:
+        return False
+    if x.dim() != 3 or x.shape[0] != 1 or not x.is_contiguous():
+        return False
+    for operand in (residual, gate, shift, scale, weight, bias):
+        if isinstance(operand, torch.Tensor) and (
+            operand.device.type != "xpu" or not operand.is_contiguous()
+        ):
+            return False
+    if residual.shape != x.shape or residual.dtype != x.dtype:
+        return False
+    hidden = x.shape[-1]
+    if hidden > MAX_FUSED_HIDDEN:
+        return False
+    if isinstance(gate, torch.Tensor):
+        if gate.dim() not in (3, 4) or gate.shape[0] != 1 or gate.shape[-1] != hidden:
+            return False
+        if gate.dim() == 3:
+            if gate.shape[1] != 1:
+                return False
+        elif (
+            gate.shape[2] != 1 or gate.shape[1] <= 0 or x.shape[1] % gate.shape[1] != 0
+        ):
+            return False
+    elif type(gate) is not int or gate != 1:
+        return False
+    for modulation in (scale, shift):
+        if not isinstance(modulation, torch.Tensor):
+            return False
+        if modulation.numel() not in (1, hidden):
+            return False
+    for affine in (weight, bias):
+        if affine is not None and affine.numel() != hidden:
+            return False
+    params = (gate, shift, scale, weight, bias)
+    dtypes = {p.dtype for p in params if isinstance(p, torch.Tensor)}
+    return len(dtypes) == 1 and shift.dtype in _SUPPORTED_DTYPES

@@ -0,0 +1,88 @@
+import sgl_kernel  # noqa: F401
+import torch
+
+from sglang.kernels.ops.diffusion.norm.scale_residual_norm_scale_shift_triton import (
+    can_use_fused_scale_residual_norm_scale_shift_triton,
+)
+from sglang.srt.utils.patch_torch import register_fake_if_exists
+
+_fused_scale_residual_norm_scale_shift = (
+    torch.ops.sgl_kernel.fused_scale_residual_norm_scale_shift
+)
+
+
+def _param_dtype(
+    *, gate: torch.Tensor | int, weight: torch.Tensor | None, shift: torch.Tensor
+) -> torch.dtype:
+    if weight is not None:
+        return weight.dtype
+    if isinstance(gate, torch.Tensor):
+        return gate.dtype
+    return shift.dtype
+
+
+def can_use_fused_scale_residual_norm_scale_shift_sycl(
+    *,
+    residual: torch.Tensor,
+    x: torch.Tensor,
+    gate: torch.Tensor | int,
+    shift: torch.Tensor,
+    scale: torch.Tensor,
+    weight: torch.Tensor | None,
+    bias: torch.Tensor | None,
+) -> bool:
+    if not can_use_fused_scale_residual_norm_scale_shift_triton(
+        residual=residual,
+        x=x,
+        gate=gate,
+        shift=shift,
+        scale=scale,
+        weight=weight,
+        bias=bias,
+    ):
+        return False
+    dtypes = {p.dtype for p in (gate, weight, bias) if isinstance(p, torch.Tensor)}
+    if len(dtypes) > 1:
+        return False
+    param_dtype = _param_dtype(gate=gate, weight=weight, shift=shift)
+    return all(
+        m.dtype == param_dtype or param_dtype == torch.float32 for m in (shift, scale)
+    )
+
+
+def fused_scale_residual_norm_scale_shift_sycl(
+    *,
+    residual: torch.Tensor,
+    x: torch.Tensor,
+    gate: torch.Tensor | int,
+    shift: torch.Tensor,
+    scale: torch.Tensor,
+    weight: torch.Tensor | None,
+    bias: torch.Tensor | None,
+    eps: float,
+) -> tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor]:
+    param_dtype = _param_dtype(gate=gate, weight=weight, shift=shift)
+    return _fused_scale_residual_norm_scale_shift(
+        residual,
+        x,
+        gate if isinstance(gate, torch.Tensor) else None,
+        weight,
+        bias,
+        scale.to(param_dtype),
+        shift.to(param_dtype),
+        eps,
+    )
+
+
+@register_fake_if_exists("sgl_kernel::fused_scale_residual_norm_scale_shift")
+def _(
+    residual: torch.Tensor,
+    x: torch.Tensor,
+    gate: torch.Tensor | None,
+    weight: torch.Tensor | None,
+    bias: torch.Tensor | None,
+    scale: torch.Tensor,
+    shift: torch.Tensor,
+    eps: float,
+) -> tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor]:
+    return torch.empty_like(x), torch.empty_like(x)

+    if x.dim() != 3 or x.shape[0] != 1 or not x.is_contiguous():
+        return False
+    for operand in (residual, gate, shift, scale, weight, bias):
+        if isinstance(operand, torch.Tensor) and (
+            operand.device.type != "xpu" or not operand.is_contiguous()
+        ):
+            return False
+    if residual.shape != x.shape or residual.dtype != x.dtype:
+        return False
+    hidden = x.shape[-1]
+    if hidden > MAX_FUSED_HIDDEN:
+        return False
+    if isinstance(gate, torch.Tensor):
+        if gate.dim() not in (3, 4) or gate.shape[0] != 1 or gate.shape[-1] != hidden:
+            return False
+        if gate.dim() == 3:
+            if gate.shape[1] != 1:
+                return False
+        elif (
+            gate.shape[2] != 1 or gate.shape[1] <= 0 or x.shape[1] % gate.shape[1] != 0
+        ):
+            return False
+    elif type(gate) is not int or gate != 1:
+        return False
+    for modulation in (scale, shift):
+        if not isinstance(modulation, torch.Tensor):
+            return False
+        if modulation.numel() not in (1, hidden):
+            return False
+    for affine in (weight, bias):
+        if affine is not None and affine.numel() != hidden:
+            return False
+    params = (gate, shift, scale, weight, bias)
+    dtypes = {p.dtype for p in params if isinstance(p, torch.Tensor)}
+    return len(dtypes) == 1 and shift.dtype in _SUPPORTED_DTYPES
